claims.text: A bimodal heterogeneous microstructure can overcome the conventional strength–ductility trade-off in high-entropy alloys.
Fine-grained regions contribute strength while coarse-grained regions contribute ductility.
Conventionally processed homogeneous high-entropy alloys can exhibit high strength at the expense of ductility.
Mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering can produce a refined high-entropy-alloy microstructure.
Applying HPT after mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering generates a controlled bimodal grain-size distribution.
The proposed processing route retains interconnected coarse-grained areas within fine-grained regions.
The proposed microstructure contains well-bonded interfaces between its fine- and coarse-grained regions.
Fine grains increase strength through grain-boundary strengthening and impeded dislocation motion.
Coarse grains sustain ductility by permitting more extensive plastic deformation.
Interfaces between fine- and coarse-grained regions promote strain partitioning.
Strain partitioning at fine–coarse interfaces delays crack initiation and propagation.
The bimodal alloy will exhibit an approximately 20–30% increase in yield strength relative to a homogeneous alloy.
The predicted yield-strength increase will occur while ductility is maintained or moderately improved.
The beneficial strength–ductility response depends on an optimal coarse-to-fine grain volume fraction.
An excessively high fraction of fine grains may compromise ductility.
The mechanical outcome may vary with alloy composition.
The microstructural and mechanical outcome may vary with processing parameters.
SEM or TEM can quantify grain-size distributions and verify whether fine and coarse regions coexist.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome treats maintained ductility together with increased yield strength as success, whereas the falsification rule says that a lack of statistically significant ductility improvement refutes the hypothesis. Thus, unchanged ductility is simultaneously allowed by the prediction and treated as falsifying.
